\parbox{\linewidth}{\justifying\scriptsize *Development-stage runs (before the confirmatory runs; none uses the 11 new datasets). Each run header gives the datasets, the trials per dataset, and the decisions (dev. = the 18 development datasets; (D) = the 34 confirmation datasets of the supporting group); decisions of a row in parentheses where the decisions differ. MINI-12 and MINI-14 tune HGB with Optuna (tree-structured Parzen estimator, 25 search iterations) on the 630-row SEARCH split; MINI-14 repeats this at 630, 2,000 and 5,000 tuning rows. Superscripts give the power check LOCO$_0$: a, $0.81\%$; b, $18.22\%$; c, $5.54\%$. Mean reference weighted-$F_1$ in MINI-12: $0.8180$ for the default HGB and $0.8206$ for the tuned learner, a mean gain of $+0.0026$. MINI-14, mean reference gain of the tuned learner at $630$, $2{,}000$, $5{,}000$ rows and all sizes: $+0.0027$, $+0.0021$, $+0.0020$, $+0.0023$; share of trials clearly worse: $12.3\%$, $9.0\%$, $6.7\%$, $9.3\%$. Accepted: lower bootstrap quantile above the margin 0.005; false improvement: reference gain at most 0. Bound: KL-ratio bound (b = 1); LOCO: leave-one-dataset-out. Clearly worse: the 95\% reference interval lies below zero. Power check LOCO$_0$: the LOCO bound recomputed with zero false improvements; with 50 trials per dataset it exceeds 10\% even when no decision is a false improvement (MINI-19), and 100 or more trials per dataset bring it below 10\% (MINI-02; MINI-19 extended by MINI-19b).}
